steps.user_message: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves landlord-tenant eviction case. My lawyer is Amy Foster from Caldwell Legal; we have proceedings at immigration court. The discovery phase just ended and we're waiting for a hearing date.. Opposing party: the other parent in the custody case. This is in Maricopa County, Arizona. I have documentation but I'm not sure what else the court will want. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about whether I need to get more evidence before the next date? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with legal-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
I can help with that — first, one quick clarification: you mentioned landlord–tenant eviction, immigration court, and an opposing party who’s the other parent in a custody case. Are these all part of the same matter (e.g., facts from a custody dispute are part of an immigration proceeding and an eviction), or are you juggling multiple separate cases? Tell me which case(s) you want to prepare for and whether Amy Foster is counsel for all of them. That will let me tailor the checklist precisely.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical, attorney-ready set of questions and an evidence checklist you can use right away. Use these to ask Amy Foster what else you should collect before the next hearing.

Suggested high-priority questions to ask your attorney (Amy Foster)
- Which specific case(s) should I be preparing evidence for? Please confirm docket numbers, court (immigration court? Maricopa County court?), and next scheduled steps.
- What is the scope of the upcoming hearing (status conference, pretrial, merits, custody, bond, eviction hearing, removal hearing)?
- Have we fulfilled all discovery obligations? Are there outstanding discovery requests from the other side or disclosures we must still produce?
- What evidentiary deadlines do I need to know (exhibit lists, witness lists, expert disclosures, motions in limine, pre-hearing briefs)? What are filing/service dates?
- Which facts or issues do you think are legally most important to prove at the hearing?
- What types of evidence will carry the most weight in this court (documents, sworn declarations, live witness testimony, expert reports, photos, police/medical records)?
- Do you recommend additional witness statements or sworn affidavits? If so, from whom and what should they cover?
- Do we need any expert witnesses (e.g., property/repairs expert for eviction, child psychologist for custody, country-condition expert for immigration)? If yes, what scope and what timeline to retain?
- Are there any hearsay or authentication concerns with the documents I have? Will the court require originals, certified copies, or foundation witnesses?
- Do any documents require certified translations or notarized affidavits?
- Should we subpoena records (bank, hospital, landlord records, school) or law enforcement records? If so, please prepare the subpoena now?
- Are any protective orders or sealing motions needed for sensitive records (medical, mental health, immigration, juvenile records)?
- Would you like me to prepare an exhibit packet and index for the court? What format do you prefer (electronic PDF with bookmarks, exhibit stickers/numbering for paper)?
- What are the settlement/mediation options and deadlines? Is there a tactical reason to delay collecting certain evidence or to exchange additional disclosures?
- Are there strategic pre-hearing motions we should file (motion to exclude evidence, motion to compel, motion in limine, motion for continuance)?
- What are likely outcomes and next steps after this hearing, and what evidence will best position us for them?

Document and evidence checklist (organized and ready to bring/produce)
General organization items
- Case identifiers: case number(s), judge/arbitrator name, hearing date (if known), and counsel contact info.
- Timeline: a concise chronological timeline of events (dates, times, locations) with citations to supporting documents.
- Exhibit index: numbered list of all exhibits with short descriptions and Bates or file names.
- Copies: original documents, one working copy for counsel, and one for court; PDF master with bookmarks; certified translations where required.
- Authentication: documentation of provenance (who created/captured the document and when).

Eviction / landlord–tenant specific
- Lease/rental agreement and any amendments.
- Rent payment records (receipts, bank/ACH statements, ledgers).
- Notices: 3-day/5-day/10-day notices, notice to vacate, repair requests, landlord communications.
- Photographs/videos of unit condition (with dates/time stamps).
- Repair invoices, work orders, contractor estimates, code violation notices, housing inspections.
- Communication logs: texts, emails, voicemail transcripts, written complaints.
- Police reports or municipal complaints (if any interactions occurred).
- Witness statements from neighbors, building managers, contractors.
- Evidence of tenant behavior if relevant (noise complaints, property damage).

Immigration court specific
- Identity documents: passport, birth certificate, immigration documents (I-94, prior filings, receipts).
- Status history: visa applications, removal proceedings history, prior orders.
- Relief-specific evidence (e.g., asylum: country conditions, affidavits; cancellation/adjustment: continuous presence, hardship).
- Criminal records and certified dispositions if applicable.
- Medical and mental-health records (with releases).
- Affidavits/declarations from family/community supporting credibility.
- Country condition reports, NGO/State Dept. reports, expert declarations on country situation.
- Translations and certified copies of foreign documents.

Custody / family court specific
- Parenting timeline: custody/visitation history, parenting calendar.
- Child records: school records, attendance, IEPs, medical/dental records.
- Child welfare or CPS records (if any), restraining orders, police reports.
- Communication records with the other parent (texts, emails, call logs).
- Evidence of parental fitness: employment records, housing stability, substance abuse treatment records, mental health evaluations.
- Witness statements from teachers, childcare providers, neighbors, family members.
- Photographs or videos demonstrating living conditions or caregiving.
- Proposed parenting plan and proposed visitation schedule.
- Criminal or protective-order documentation related to either parent.

Evidence quality & technical details to confirm with your attorney
- Originals vs. copies: which must be produced or brought to court?
- Sworn declarations/affidavits: who should sign them, do they need to be notarized?
- Certifications: medical records, school records, criminal dispositions often need certified copies.
- Chain of custody: photos, video, digital logs — can their origin be verified?
- Authentication witness: who can lay foundation for key documents (author, custodian)?
- Hearsay: will affidavits be admissible, or does the court require live testimony?
- Redaction and privacy: what personal identifiers should be redacted before filing?
- Electronic evidence: how to present text messages, social media posts (screenshots vs. device metadata).

Practical preparation tasks you can do now
- Create a single master folder (digital + backup) with subfolders: pleadings, discovery, exhibits, witness statements, court orders.
- Number and label exhibits consistently; prepare a printable PDF exhibit book with bookmarked index.
- Draft short, targeted affidavits for key witnesses (one page each, first-person, dated, signed).
- Gather certified translations for any non-English documents.
- Compile contact info for potential witnesses and short descriptions of what they will testify about.
- List any records you don’t have but might need (banks, landlord ledger, hospital) and ask counsel to subpoena them if appropriate.
- Note any upcoming deadlines and calendar them; ask counsel about filing lead time.

Sample short email you can send to Amy (I can draft/send if you want)
Subject: Preparing for next hearing — what additional evidence do we need?

Hi Amy — the discovery phase just closed and I want to be fully prepared for the next hearing. A few quick questions:
- Which specific court/case (docket number) should I prepare for, and do you know the likely scope of the next hearing?
- Have we met all discovery obligations? Any outstanding requests or documents the court expects from us?
- What evidence would you most like me to obtain now (specific documents, witness affidavits, expert opinions)?
- Do any documents need originals, certified copies, or certified translations?
- Should we prepare an exhibit index and sworn declarations for key witnesses? If so, what format do you prefer?
- Any other pre-hearing filings or subpoenas you recommend we do now?

I can assemble an exhibit packet and draft short affidavits — tell me which items to prioritize and I’ll get them ready. Thanks.

Want help turning this into a full draft to send to Amy, or do you want me to focus the checklist for one of those case types (eviction, immigration, custody)?
